newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony says mulling tie-up with Toyota group on LCDs.
newsitem.headline: Sony says mulling tie-up with Toyota group on LCDs.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Wednesday it is considering a tie-up with the Toyota group to make next-generation liquid crystal displays (LCD).

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported on Wednesday that Sony and Toyoda Automatic Loom Works Ltd, a group firm of Toyota Motor Corp, plan to set up a joint venture for LCD production and marketing before the end of this year.
The two companies will spend 50 billion to 60 billion yen to build a factory in Aichi Prefecture in Western Japan for making low-temperature polysilicon LCDs, the paper said.
The new factory is expected to start production as early as in the second half of the 1998/99 business year.
The Toyota group is entering the LCD business as the device may be commonly used in cars in the future in displays for navigation systems, the paper said.
A spokesman for Toyoda Automatic Loom Works said the company is talking with Sony about a possible LCD joint venture, but that nothing has been decided.
